This game has what seems to be an amazing story. I cannot enjoy it, however, due to nearly constant crashes. I have a total of 3 hours playtime at the time of this review, and it has crashed 5 times thus far.

On top of this, the performance is all over the place. The joys of PC gaming in modern times mean that you need to perform tech support to get a game up and running. I installed process lasso, and induced the performance mode for ff16 to force only p cores to do the heavy lifting. This has not resolved the crashing. During one of the iconic battles in the beginning of the game, the game managed a whopping 18 fps. This killed the immersion completely and the performance settings are disabled during the entire sequence. 

Your mileage may very, but I'm profoundly disappointed. At the time of my purchase, this is not a new PC release.

Buy at your own risk.

FFXVI isn’t just a game—it’s a masterpiece. The story is dark, emotional, and utterly immersive, with Clive Rosfield delivering one of the most unforgettable journeys in gaming. Every cutscene feels like a reward, every twist hits like a gut punch, and the characters? Absolute perfection.

The combat? A dream come true for action fans. It’s fast, brutal, and endlessly satisfying. And don’t get me started on the boss fights- they’re massive, cinematic, and left me breathless every single time.

As a lifelong fan, this game didn’t just meet my expectations—it blew them out of the water. Every moment feels crafted with love and passion, and it shows. FFXVI is more than a game- it’s a reminder of why I fell in love with Final Fantasy in the first place.

I really wanted to recommend this game, but the poor PC port ruins the entire experience.
Almost all of my playtime has been spent trying to fix technical issues instead of actually enjoying the game.

Every time a cutscene starts, I can only cross my fingers and hope it doesn’t crash.

Do you know the definition of insanity?
Trying to fix the same problem over and over again, expecting a different result.

I’ve attempted every possible solution — again, again, and again.
At this point, I’m going to purchase the PS5 version instead. I’m simply exhausted.

Square Enix, please fix this game and deliver a proper PC port for your future Final Fantasy titles.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
My PC specs for reference:

CPU: AMD R9-9950X3D (with ASUS RYUJIN 360 AIO)
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5090 (with latest drivers)
RAM: Kingston Predator 64GB(32gigs*2) DDR5 6000MHz
PSU: MSI 1250W
OS: Windows 11 64-bit (with latest update)

Playing at 4K 60FPS on PC looks fantastic — when it works.
But crashing during almost every cutscene?
Honestly, I’d rather play the PS5 version with dynamic resolution and some blur than deal with constant instability.

Square Enix, please fix this game and give PC players the quality port we deserve.

A game that knows what it is and executes it almost flawlessly. Great story, extremely fun combat. Just a very streamlined experience overall.

The only complaint that I wouldn't call a nitpick is that that that I'm not super stoked to replay it in "hard mode" because it's so story heavy. But I'm not a big fan of rewatching movies either, so some people might not be bothered by that.

Story wise: A solid well acted story with a lot of really heartfelt moments and a surprisingly mature tone/characters for a FF game. There were tears at the end for sure. This and the spectacle moments is what will keep you playing much more than the side quests or combat mechanics.

Gameplay wise: Combat and systems are kind of pulling a lot of influence from god of war's combat systems and you can draw a lot of paralells between eikons and weapons, skills and weapon runes, doggo and boy... It was fun, but lacked a lot of depth and customisability that I personally think of when I think of Final Fantasy. Like you can literally ignore all the accessory equipment in this game as they are all either small cooldown buffs or small damage buffs for the different abilities, and that's kinda it. 
Overall I think I enjoyed combat in 16 more than I did in 15, but I still prefer classic turn based combat and deeper RPG systems as per 7, 8, 9, and 10.

Overall it's an easy recommend just for the story and spectacle of it and dispite the combat being pretty simple, it also doesn't get in the way of enjoying it (like FF7 remake did a lot of times.)

If you are expecting an old school Final Fantasy experience you won't get it with Final Fantasy XVI. This game's story is brutal and f bombs are dropped left and right. It lacks much of the humor and charm of the older Final Fantasy titles. And obviously the turn based combat of old is gone. But for all that I do enjoy this game. Elements of Final Fantasy still exist in this world (chocobos, moogles, and eikons (summons)). The difficulty is average on the "Action Focused" game (you have the option of choosing Action Focused or Story Focused at the beginning) with general enemies being a cake walk but some bosses posing more of a challenge. That being said I have yet to die/game over once. The story is where this game shines. The world building is superb and is actually hard to keep up with but many features in game allow you to go back and revist parts of the story to stay on top of it. Overall I would give this game a 9/10 and I don't regret buying it (if you are unsure play the demo first, that is what I did and that got me hooked).

This ain't a game dawg, it's a movie. Literally half of the game is cutscenes, and every single one of them is absolute cinema. The cinematography, voice acting, and sound design all go insanely hard. Personally, my favorite scene were the Bahamut fight and the ending, which was totally not an insanely emotional for me. Anyway. But even though the story is absolutely incredible, the gameplay ends up feeling kinda lacking. The Eikon battles are insanely spectacular, but the regular human combat is just okay. It's not bad, but it's not amazing either. It's kinda unfortunate because the majority of the fights are human battles rather than Eikon battles.

Overall, though, it's still a fantastic game that's absolutely worth playing👍.
